agreements.TERMS_OF_SERVICE.detailHtml:
Workaway Terms of Service

Chapter 1. General provisions

Article 1. Purpose

These terms define the conditions and procedures for use, and the rights, obligations, responsibilities and other matters between Workaway (the “Company”) and members using the services operated by the Company.

Article 2. Definitions

The following definitions apply in these terms.

1. “Services” means services that classify, process and aggregate materials registered by individuals for purposes such as seeking work, information about guesthouse recruitment, other information searches, accommodation reservations and all other services provided through the site.

2. “Site” means the virtual place of business established using computers and telecommunications equipment, and all media through which the Company provides services, including websites, mobile websites and applications accessible through one integrated member account (ID and password).

3. “Member” means an individual who uses or intends to use the services, has entered into or intends to enter into a service agreement with the Company, and has completed registration, including setting an ID and password.

4. “ID” means the combination of letters and numbers selected by the member and assigned by the Company at registration to identify the member and enable service use.

5. “Password” means the combination of letters and numbers selected by the member when setting the ID under paragraph 4, to verify the identity of the person assigned that ID and protect the member’s rights and interests.

6. “Non-member” means a person who uses or intends to use the services without registering.

7. “User” means a person using the services, including members and non-members.

Article 3. Publication and effect of the terms

  • These terms apply to everyone wishing to use the services. Anyone who does not agree to or comply with them is prohibited from accessing and using all services operated by the Company.
  • Users accessing and using the services must review and comply with these terms and related operating policies.
  • The Company must make these terms, its business name, business address, representative’s name, business registration number and contact details available on the initial screen or notify users by other means so that users can review them.
  • The Company may amend these terms within the limits of applicable laws, including the Act on the Regulation of Terms and Conditions, the Framework Act on Telecommunications, the Framework Act on Consumers, the Act on Promotion of Information and Communications Network Utilization and Information Protection, and the Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce.
  • When amending the terms, the Company will announce the effective date and reasons from seven days before the effective date until the preceding day. Amendments unfavorable to members will be announced in the same manner from 30 days before the effective date.
  • Members may reject the amended terms within 15 days of the amendment, stop using the services and terminate the agreement. Continued use without expressly rejecting the amendment, or the passage of 15 days after the amendment, will be treated as agreement to the amended terms.
  • In the preceding case, the Company must announce the amended terms and notify members that they may reject them within 15 days after the effective date and that failure to do so will be treated as agreement.
  • Members must exercise due care regarding amendments. The Company is not responsible for losses caused by a member’s failure to review amended terms after the Company has fulfilled its obligations under this article.

Article 4. Interpretation

  • Matters not covered by these terms are governed by applicable laws, including the Act on the Regulation of Terms and Conditions, the Framework Act on Telecommunications, the Framework Act on Consumers, the Act on Promotion of Information and Communications Network Utilization and Information Protection, and the Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce. Limitations on the Company’s liability apply to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law.
  • The Company may establish separate terms or policies for individual services or service items. If they conflict with these terms, the separate terms or policies take precedence.
  • If a member uses the services under an individual agreement with the Company, that agreement takes precedence.

Chapter 2. Formation of the agreement and rights and obligations concerning member information

Article 5. Formation of the service agreement

  • The service agreement is formed when a person wishing to become a member (the “Applicant”) completes the prescribed registration form and the Company accepts the application. Clicking agree or confirm after reading these terms and the privacy policy during registration is treated as agreement to these terms.
  • Depending on the membership type, the Company may request real-name and identity verification through a specialized agency. The member must provide the name, date of birth, contact details and other information required for verification.
  • When applying through an external service, the agreement is formed when the member clicks agree or confirm regarding these terms, the privacy policy and the Company’s access to and use of the external account information required to provide the services, and the Company notifies the member through an online notice and email.

Article 6. Acceptance and restrictions on registration

The Company may refuse registration, or terminate an agreement if the following circumstances are discovered after formation:

1. Member information is false, incomplete or incorrect.

2. Another person’s name, email address, contact details or other personal information has been misappropriated.

3. The application violates applicable law or is intended to undermine public order or accepted morals.

4. Membership has been revoked under these terms within the past five years, unless the Company approves re-registration.

5. The member information duplicates that of an existing member.

6. The applicant is under 14. The Company may refuse even if a legal representative consents.

The Company may defer acceptance until the following circumstances are resolved:

1. The Company’s facilities lack available capacity.

2. Technical difficulties prevent service provision.

3. Real-name and identity verification under Article 5, paragraph 2 is in progress.

Article 7. Management of member information

  • Members may view and correct their personal information through the service’s editing function or customer support.
  • Members must update registered information when it changes. Members bear disadvantages caused by failing to update it, and the Company is not responsible unless it acted intentionally or with gross negligence.
  • Resumes are registered and provided in the form requested when created or edited.
  • Members are responsible for managing their accounts and may not transfer or lend them to others.

Article 8. Collection and protection of member information

  • The Company complies with personal information laws when collecting, using, retaining and providing member information.
  • In addition to information provided directly by members, the Company may collect, use or provide other information to third parties through procedures prescribed by privacy laws. It will obtain the required consent or follow the legally prescribed procedures.
  • The Company endeavors to protect members’ personal information as required by privacy laws. Details of its processing practices are always available in the privacy policy.

Chapter 3. Use of the services

Article 9. Service use

  • Anyone may use the services. Non-members must also review and comply with these terms. The Company is not responsible for losses caused by failure to comply.
  • These terms apply to non-members through actions such as accessing and browsing the services.

Article 10. Service content

  • The Company provides the services in Article 2, paragraph 1, including the following. Available services and functions may vary at the time of use.
    • 1. Guesthouse information search, reservations and payments.
  • The Company may add or change service content as necessary.
  • The Company may discontinue all or part of the services because of difficulty providing them smoothly, deteriorating profitability, operational or technical needs, or the circumstances in Article 12, paragraph 2.
  • In the cases under paragraphs 2 and 3, the Company must notify members of additions, changes or reasons for discontinuation through in-app notices.
  • Detailed guidance and information are provided through service operating policies and individual pages.
  • No separate compensation is provided when all or part of the services end or are discontinued, except:
    • 1. Where applicable law, separate terms or policies provide otherwise.
    • 2. Where a reservation made before service termination is canceled for reasons attributable to the Company.

Article 11. Fees

  • The services in Article 10, paragraph 1 are free. Some other services may become paid services, in which case changes, including fees, will be announced in the manner specified in paragraph 4 of that article.
  • The Company may change paid-service fees without prior notice. Changes do not apply retroactively to previously applicable amounts.

Article 12. Changes and suspension

  • The Company may add or change services after notifying members of the changes and effective date as specified in Article 10.
  • The Company may suspend all or part of the services in the following cases:
    • 1. Regular system maintenance, server expansion or replacement, or other operational needs.
    • 2. Normal provision is difficult because of equipment failure, excessive demand or suspension of telecommunications services by a carrier.
    • 3. Natural disasters, national emergencies or other force majeure.
    • 4. Other serious reasons make continued provision inappropriate.
  • The Company will notify members in the manner specified in Article 10 when suspending services under the preceding paragraph, unless notification is impossible, such as a suspension caused by circumstances outside its control.
  • The Company is not responsible for problems arising from a suspension under paragraph 2 that occurred without its intent or negligence.

Article 13. Information and advertising

  • The Company may place advertisements on service screens and spaces in connection with its operations.
  • The Company is not responsible for losses, damages or disputes with advertisers arising from users’ use of advertisements or goods promoted through the services. It is responsible to the extent of its intent or gross negligence in providing the services.

Article 14. Ownership of rights

  • Copyright and intellectual property rights in the services belong to the Company.
  • The Company owns or is licensed to use copyright and other intellectual property rights in its service designs, original text, graphics, trademarks, marks and logos.
  • The Company may hold users responsible for commercially using information obtained through the services, or allowing third parties to do so, without prior approval.

Chapter 4. Obligations of the Company and users

Article 15. Company obligations

  • The Company will not engage in conduct prohibited by law and will make its best efforts to provide continuous, stable services under these terms.
  • The Company will maintain privacy protection systems, comply with its privacy policy and not disclose or distribute users’ personal information to third parties without consent.
  • The Company must take necessary action on legitimate service-related opinions from users.
  • The Company is liable only where users suffer damage from its services through its intent or gross negligence.
  • When disputes arise between users, the Company must act under applicable laws, including electronic commerce laws, and inform users of the handling procedure.

Article 16. User obligations

  • Members must comply with applicable law, these terms and Company notices, and must not interfere with the Company’s work.
  • Users must review the detailed information and transaction conditions before paying through the services. The Company is not responsible for losses resulting from failure to review them accurately.
  • Members using credit cards must prevent loss of passwords and other information themselves. The Company is responsible for information loss caused by service defects.
  • Users may not transfer, give away or pledge their service-use rights or position under the agreement.
  • Members must not engage in the following:
    • 1. Entering or transmitting false information during identity verification or service use.
    • 2. Misappropriating another member’s information to use the services improperly.
    • 3. Intentionally cutting off contact with the Company or guesthouse members.
    • 4. Collecting, storing or disclosing another member’s personal information without consent.
    • 5. Conduct intended for or related to criminal activity.
    • 6. Defaming or insulting other members.
    • 7. Infringing the Company’s intellectual property or other rights.
    • 8. Hacking or distributing viruses through the services.
    • 9. Conduct deemed to interfere, or likely to interfere, with stable operation.
    • 10. Commercial activities using site information and services.
    • 11. Impersonating Company employees, service administrators or operators.
    • 12. Other conduct contrary to accepted morals, public order or applicable law.

Article 17. Termination

  • Members may request termination by following the method provided through the services or related pages.
  • The Company must terminate the member’s agreement upon receiving the request.
  • Members must complete all reservations and use before requesting termination. If requesting termination earlier, they must withdraw or cancel those reservations and bear any resulting disadvantages.
  • The Company may terminate an agreement or delete a member’s resume without prior consent in the following cases:
    • 1. Failure to faithfully fulfill member obligations.
    • 2. Failure to pay prescribed paid-service fees.
    • 3. Use of information outside the service’s purpose that causes social controversy.
    • 4. Registered information is untrue or manipulated.
    • 5. Defamation of the Company or a third party in connection with the services.
    • 6. Other circumstances equivalent to those above.
    • 7. Member information is found to be false or registered in another person’s name.
    • 8. The information is confirmed to concern a child under 14.
  • After termination, personal information is deleted seven days after the termination date, except information the Company may retain under applicable law and the privacy policy.

Article 18. Damages

  • The Company must compensate members for damage caused by its violation of these terms or other reasons attributable to it in connection with its services.
  • The Company must compensate members for damage caused by inaccurate information provided for reasons attributable to it.
  • Members must compensate the Company and third parties for damage caused by their violation of these terms or other reasons attributable to them.
  • The Company is not liable for a member’s losses caused by another member.

Article 19. Protection of personal information

The Company must endeavor to protect members’ personal information, comply with the Act on Promotion of Information and Communications Network Utilization and Information Protection and the Personal Information Protection Act, and publish its privacy policy on the site.

Article 20. Consent to provision and use of credit information

  • Before providing or using personal credit information obtained during registration, the Company must disclose the reasons and the relevant institution or business and obtain the member’s consent under Article 23 of the Credit Information Use and Protection Act.
  • Where a member has consented to third-party provision and use under that Act in connection with these services, the member is deemed to consent to the Company providing information to credit information businesses or credit information collection agencies for credit assessment, or to public institutions for policy purposes.

Article 21. Disclaimer

  • The Company is exempt from responsibility for service provision where natural disasters, circumstances outside its control or other force majeure prevent provision or cause suspension or interruption.
  • The Company is not responsible for service disruption attributable to members.
  • The Company is not responsible for losses or damages arising from transactions through the services between users or between users and third parties.
  • The Company is not responsible for damage caused by information obtained through the services.
  • The Company is not responsible for the content of user posts, such as reviews or guesthouse ratings.
  • Products are managed under the seller’s responsibility. Except for service-operation problems, liability for product defects or deficiencies belongs to the seller rather than the Company.
  • The Company has no duty to monitor, and is not responsible for, the content or quality of advertised products, except within its obligations for provisional measures under the Information and Communications Network Act.
  • Unless the Company, its employees or representative acted intentionally or with gross negligence, the Company is not responsible for damage arising from:
    • 1. False or inaccurate member information.
    • 2. Illegal access to or use of servers by third parties, including members.
    • 3. Illegal interference with or interruption of transmissions to or from servers.
    • 4. Viruses or other malicious programs transmitted or distributed by third parties through the services.

Article 22. Dispute resolution

  • The Company and members must make every effort necessary to resolve service-related disputes amicably.
  • Despite those efforts, the Seoul Central District Court has jurisdiction over litigation concerning service use.

agreements.GUESTHOUSE_RESERVATION_POLICY:
Accommodation cancellation and refund rules

{{guesthouseName}}

Up to 7 days before check-in0% deducted from the total payment
7–3 days before check-in0% deducted from the total payment
3–1 days before check-in0% deducted from the total payment
1 day before check-in100% deducted from the total payment
Check-in dayNo cancellation or refund
  • Cancellation fee rates are based on the check-in date.
  • For consecutive stays of two or more nights, the fee rate based on the reservation’s check-in date applies to the entire amount.
  • Some properties apply their own cancellation and refund policies. Check whether cancellation fees apply for each period before booking.
  • Fees are calculated from the full reservation amount before coupon or point discounts. See the calculation rules below.

Cancellation fee calculation

Fees are applied in this order:

  1. Cash, payment gateway and simplified-payment amounts.
  2. Workaway points used.
  3. Coupon discounts.
  • If the fee exceeds the amount actually paid (cash/payment gateway/simplified payment plus points), any necessary coupon return for the excess is determined by the coupon return policy applicable to the reservation.
  • The same policy applies to cancellations made to change dates, rooms or other reservation details.

Exceptions

  • Reservations made after the check-in time: within 10 minutes of reservation completion.
  • However, cancellation and refunds may be unavailable after the check-in time or for certain accommodation products, even within 10 minutes of completion.

Natural disasters or severe weather

  • If force majeure, including natural disasters or severe weather, prevents service use, contact the property directly.
  • You may be asked for evidence of the impact, including on-site conditions, transportation and travel routes. Cancellation and refunds may be unavailable depending on the severity of the disaster.

When cancellation is unavailable

Reservations and payments cannot be canceled or refunded in the following cases:

  • After the check-in time, including no-shows, or after actual check-in.
  • No-show: not using the reserved property without prior notice.
  • Cancellation on the check-in day.
  • Stays by minors.
  • Under the Youth Protection Act, mixed-gender stays by minors under 19 are prohibited, and mixed-gender stays without an accompanying legal representative are not permitted.
  • Rooms without parking or intended for guests arriving on foot.
  • After cancellation becomes unavailable, lack of parking is not grounds for cancellation.

Other notices

  • Real-time booking can result in duplicate reservations for a room. The first completed payment takes priority and later duplicate reservations may be canceled.
  • Reservations may be canceled after customer support notification if peak-season rates are not finalized or a rate was entered incorrectly.
  • If the facilities differ from the information shown when booking or the contract is performed differently, the reservation may be canceled at the guest’s or property’s request.
  • Cancellation and refunds follow each property’s policy.
  • Workaway is an e-commerce intermediary, not a party to the accommodation sale. It does not handle cancellation/refund requests or disputes arising on site with properties, and is not liable for direct or indirect losses caused by natural disasters, accommodation-industry strikes, airline circumstances, civil unrest or other such reasons.
  • This product is for the purchaser’s personal use. Commercial resale or transfer is strictly prohibited. If prohibited resale is confirmed, the Company may cancel the reservation and restrict further purchases. Penalties and fees incurred in that case are not refunded.

Refund methods

  • Reversal to the original payment method takes 3–7 business days after cancellation is completed.
  • If the selected payment method cannot receive a refund, customer support may arrange a bank transfer instead.
  • A bank-transfer refund may take 3–5 business days to reach your account.
  • Mobile-phone-billed payments can be reversed and refunded only within the original payment month.
  • Refunds use the original payment method. If that is not possible, such as cancellation in a later month, the refund is paid in cash by bank transfer. At the customer’s request, a refund may instead be made in Workaway points.

Return of used coupons

  • Coupons owned by the customer are returned to the account when the reservation is canceled, regardless of cancellation fees.
  • Instant-discount coupons (first-come coupons) are excluded because they are not coupons owned by the member.

Accommodation rules

- Comply with each property’s rules and terms. Violations may result in refusal of check-in, removal or extra charges. The person booking and using the property bears responsibility and must check the rules and facilities.
- Exceeding the permitted occupancy may result in refusal of use or extra charges, for which the person booking and using the property is responsible.
- Reservations are made in real time. Even a reservation confirmed at booking may become pending or canceled due to overbooking or other property circumstances. Payments will be refunded automatically.
- Under the Youth Protection Act and related laws, mixed-gender stays by minors under 19 are prohibited, and mixed-gender stays without an accompanying legal representative are not permitted. If check-in is refused for this reason, cancellation and refunds are unavailable.
- Property information is provided as a booking reference and may differ from actual conditions due to changes or other reasons. Workaway is not responsible unless the discrepancy is attributable to it, such as failure to accurately reflect photos or information supplied by partner sellers.
- Room-assignment requests, such as non-smoking rooms or high floors, are passed to the property. The property makes the final decision, and Workaway cannot guarantee fulfillment.

Accommodation cancellation and refund rules
  {{guesthouseName}} 

    Up to 7 days before check-in  0% deducted from the total payment 
  7–3 days before check-in  0% deducted from the total payment 
  3–1 days before check-in  0% deducted from the total payment 
  1 day before check-in  100% deducted from the total payment 
  Check-in day  No cancellation or refund 
  
  Cancellation fee rates are based on the check-in date.
 For consecutive stays of two or more nights, the fee rate based on the reservation’s check-in date applies to the entire amount.
 Some properties apply their own cancellation and refund policies. Check whether cancellation fees apply for each period before booking.
 Fees are calculated from the full reservation amount before coupon or point discounts. See the calculation rules below.


 Cancellation fee calculation
 Fees are applied in this order:
  Cash, payment gateway and simplified-payment amounts.
 Workaway points used.
 Coupon discounts.


  If the fee exceeds the amount actually paid (cash/payment gateway/simplified payment plus points), any necessary coupon return for the excess is determined by the coupon return policy applicable to the reservation.
 The same policy applies to cancellations made to change dates, rooms or other reservation details.


 Exceptions
  Reservations made after the check-in time: within 10 minutes of reservation completion.
 However, cancellation and refunds may be unavailable after the check-in time or for certain accommodation products, even within 10 minutes of completion.


 Natural disasters or severe weather
  If force majeure, including natural disasters or severe weather, prevents service use, contact the property directly.
 You may be asked for evidence of the impact, including on-site conditions, transportation and travel routes. Cancellation and refunds may be unavailable depending on the severity of the disaster.


 When cancellation is unavailable
 Reservations and payments cannot be canceled or refunded in the following cases:

  After the check-in time, including no-shows, or after actual check-in.
 No-show: not using the reserved property without prior notice.
 Cancellation on the check-in day.
 Stays by minors.
 Under the Youth Protection Act, mixed-gender stays by minors under 19 are prohibited, and mixed-gender stays without an accompanying legal representative are not permitted.
 Rooms without parking or intended for guests arriving on foot.
 After cancellation becomes unavailable, lack of parking is not grounds for cancellation.


 Other notices
  Real-time booking can result in duplicate reservations for a room. The first completed payment takes priority and later duplicate reservations may be canceled.
 Reservations may be canceled after customer support notification if peak-season rates are not finalized or a rate was entered incorrectly.
 If the facilities differ from the information shown when booking or the contract is performed differently, the reservation may be canceled at the guest’s or property’s request.
 Cancellation and refunds follow each property’s policy.
 Workaway is an e-commerce intermediary, not a party to the accommodation sale. It does not handle cancellation/refund requests or disputes arising on site with properties, and is not liable for direct or indirect losses caused by natural disasters, accommodation-industry strikes, airline circumstances, civil unrest or other such reasons.
 This product is for the purchaser’s personal use. Commercial resale or transfer is strictly prohibited. If prohibited resale is confirmed, the Company may cancel the reservation and restrict further purchases. Penalties and fees incurred in that case are not refunded.


 Refund methods
  Reversal to the original payment method takes 3–7 business days after cancellation is completed.
 If the selected payment method cannot receive a refund, customer support may arrange a bank transfer instead.
 A bank-transfer refund may take 3–5 business days to reach your account.
 Mobile-phone-billed payments can be reversed and refunded only within the original payment month.
 Refunds use the original payment method. If that is not possible, such as cancellation in a later month, the refund is paid in cash by bank transfer. At the customer’s request, a refund may instead be made in Workaway points.


 Return of used coupons
  Coupons owned by the customer are returned to the account when the reservation is canceled, regardless of cancellation fees.
 Instant-discount coupons (first-come coupons) are excluded because they are not coupons owned by the member.

agreements.LOCATION_BASED_SERVICE.detail:
Consent to location-based service terms

Workaway uses your location to provide more accurate information about nearby accommodation and jobs.

Collection and use of location information

  • Location information is collected through your smartphone’s GPS, Wi-Fi and telecommunications networks.
  • Collected locations are used for:
    • Guesthouse recommendations and guidance based on your current location.
    • Distance filters, such as distance to a workplace.
    • Local promotions and benefits.

Your rights

  • You may allow or refuse location collection at any time in app settings.
  • WA does not store real-time location or use it for purposes other than those stated.
  • Collected information is encrypted, stored securely and not provided externally.

You can use Workaway’s basic functions without location-based services.
